title: Part Finder
description: Find a per cent of a number or a measure from a benchmark, from lots of 10%, or as the per cent over 100 times the number, and lift the used part away to see what is left.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Find a per cent of a number from a benchmark, from lots of 10% or as the per cent over 100 times the number, find a per cent of a measure in the unit asked for, and find what is left after a per cent is used.
writeup.look: A whole bar labelled 100% across the working area, with the Fold and Cut into ten buttons over it. The fraction line lies under the bar, and the Unit fact card and the Use button join on the later phases.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Part Finder' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the per cent of the bar that is lit. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The whole bar lies at x 110, y 300, 900 long and 90 tall, labelled Whole and 100% at its right end, the quantity written on it in deep blue. The Fold buttons, Half, Quarter and Tenth, the Double button and the Cut into ten button sit in a row above it at y 220, each labelled in words. Folds and cuts draw near-black lines across the bar, every part exactly one width, each labelled with its share. Parts lit by dragging turn amber and are counted in lots of ten per cent in the running count. The fraction line lies under the bar at x 110, y 430, working the per cent over one hundred times the quantity step by step; when Double lays a second whole bar of the same length under the first, the fraction line drops to y 520. The Unit fact card stands at x 110, y 560, its fact in violet. On the fourth phase the Use button stands at x 700, y 560, the used part lifts off the bar in rose, labelled Used, down to y 640, and the part that stays is green, labelled Left. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key, a % key and unit keys for g, kg, mL, litres, cm, m and km. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. The part the question gives, as shaded cells, a fraction, a decimal or an amount, is deep blue, labelled Given. The per cent, fraction or decimal the working reaches, and what is left after a part is used, is green, labelled Answer or Left. Both terms multiplied or divided by one number, and the times one hundred step before the % sign, are vermilion, labelled Both terms or Times 100. A unit fact that puts two amounts in one unit is violet, labelled Unit fact. The part used, taken away or not won is rose, labelled Used or Not won. The step, cell or number being worked on now is amber. A zero holding a place open inside a decimal is grey, labelled Place holder, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded cell of a whole stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the % sign is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The bar shows the last quantity with its part lit, the unit fact that was used, and the part left in green.

phases.win: one quarter lit amber, and the answer card reads 25% of 60 is 15
phases.does: taps Quarter, reads one of the four equal parts, and types it
phases.goal: 50% is half, 25% is a quarter, 10% is a tenth and 200% is double
phases.says: Twenty-five per cent is a quarter. Fold the bar into four.
phases.check: Away from the screen: what is fifty per cent of the children in your class?
phases.feels: the bar falling into equal parts, each with its share written on it
phases.hands: Fold a paper strip in half, then in quarters, and write fifty per cent and twenty-five per cent on the folds. Share a pile of counters the same way.
phases.tries: First rung: fold the bar in half and read one part. Second rung: fold each half again and read one part. Third rung: the same task with a quantity that shares evenly, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: halving is the fold the hands know best
wrong.move: folds into halves when a quarter is asked for
wrong.screen: the half fold is kept, and a second fold line in amber cuts each half again, with the four parts numbered

wrong.why: the fold made the parts, so their count is what shows
wrong.move: reads the number of parts instead of one part's share
wrong.screen: one part lights amber and its share is written on it, beside the count of parts

phases.screen: the bar holding 60, and the question card asking for 25% of it
phases.soWhat: fifty per cent is half, twenty-five per cent a quarter, ten per cent a tenth and two hundred per cent double

phases.win: four parts of eight lit, and both routes read 40% of 80 is 32
phases.does: taps Cut into ten, lights four parts, and checks with the fraction line
phases.goal: a per cent of a number is found from lots of 10%, or as the per cent over 100 times the number
phases.says: Find ten per cent first. How many lots of it do you need?
phases.check: Away from the screen: how would you find seventy per cent of something, if you knew ten per cent of it?
phases.feels: lots of ten per cent stacking up to the per cent asked for
phases.hands: Cut a paper strip into ten equal parts, write the quantity's tenth on each, and colour as many parts as the tens in the per cent.
phases.tries: First rung: find ten per cent of the quantity. Second rung: find two lots of it. Third rung: the same task with a quantity that is a count of tens, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: finding ten per cent felt like the answer
wrong.screen: the lit part is counted as one lot, and the parts still needed are outlined in amber, one after another

wrong.why: the lit parts are what the finger touched
wrong.move: counts the lit parts, not their shares
wrong.screen: each lit part's share is written on it, and the shares are added along the fraction line

phases.screen: the bar holding 80, and the question card asking for 40% of it
phases.soWhat: a per cent of a number is found from lots of ten per cent, or as the per cent over one hundred times the number

phases.win: the bar reads 2000 m in violet, and the answer card reads 20% of 2 km is 400 m
phases.does: picks the Unit fact card, watches the bar relabel, then finds the per cent
phases.goal: write the measure in the unit the answer asks for, then find the per cent
phases.says: Which unit does the answer want? Change the measure first.
phases.check: Away from the screen: how many metres are in two kilometres, and which fact tells you?
phases.feels: the measure changing its unit before anything is worked
phases.hands: Lay a metre stick beside a centimetre ruler, write the unit fact, then find a per cent of the length in centimetres.
phases.tries: First rung: pick the unit fact card and rewrite the measure. Second rung: find ten per cent of the new measure. Third rung: the same task with a measure of one whole unit, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the number came out, so the unit seems a label to add
wrong.move: finds the per cent in the old unit and writes the new unit after it
wrong.screen: the Unit fact card pulses, the bar is relabelled in violet in the unit asked for, and the child's number is written against the new bar, far too small

wrong.why: several facts on the card list look alike
wrong.move: picks a unit fact that does not join the two units
wrong.screen: the chosen fact is written in violet beside the bar with its two unit words lit amber, and the fact that joins the question's units is lit on the list

phases.screen: the bar holding 2 km, and the question card asking how many metres 20% of it is
phases.soWhat: write the measure in the unit the answer asks for, then find the per cent

phases.win: 240 g lifted off in rose, and 560 g left in green, labelled Left
phases.does: lights the part used, taps Use, and reads the green part that stays
phases.goal: what is left is the whole take away the part used, and the question says which one it asks for
phases.says: Which part does the question ask for, the part used or the part left?
phases.check: Away from the screen: if thirty per cent of a jug of water is poured out, what per cent is still in the jug?
phases.feels: the used part lifting off and the part left glowing green
phases.hands: Measure some rice or water, take a per cent of it away into another bowl, and measure both parts. Say which one the question asked for.
phases.tries: First rung: light the part used and read it. Second rung: tap Use and read the part left. Third rung: the same task with a per cent that is a count of tens, before the question's own returns.

wrong.move: gives the part used when the question asks what is left
wrong.screen: the rose part labelled Used and the green part labelled Left are both written with their amounts, and the question's last words are lit amber

wrong.screen: the per cent is written over one hundred on the fraction line, and its share of the bar is lit before anything is taken away

phases.screen: the bar holding 800 g of flour, and the question card asking how much is left after 30% is used
phases.soWhat: what is left is the whole take away the part used, and the question says which one it asks for

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, when Use is tapped, the rose part lifts gently off the bar and floats down, and the green part left behind glows once with its label Left.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing lit. On the first phase the whole bar holds a number and the Fold buttons wait over it. On the second the bar holds a number with the Cut into ten button lit. On the third it holds a measure in one unit, and the question card asks for another unit. On the fourth it holds a measure of something to be used, with the Use button waiting. One thing moves, once: the first button the phase needs gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: A quantity of the child's own, folded, cut into tenths, rewritten in another unit, or used and left. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on benchmark per cents, a per cent of a number, a per cent of a measure, and what is left.

observations.why: fifty per cent is fifty hundredths, which is a half.
observations.soWhat: the benchmark per cents are a half, a quarter, a tenth and double.
observations.observe: Half of the bar was always one of two equal parts, whatever the quantity.

observations.why: ten equal parts of a whole are tenths, and a tenth is ten hundredths.
observations.soWhat: a per cent that is a count of tens is found from ten per cent first.
observations.observe: Each part of the bar cut into ten was ten per cent of it.

observations.why: the question asked for the answer in another unit.
observations.soWhat: a measure is written in the unit the answer asks for first, and the fact is said.
observations.observe: The Unit fact card had to be used before the fraction line would work.

observations.why: the part used and the part left make up the whole.
observations.soWhat: what is left is the whole take away the part used, and the question says which one it wants.
observations.observe: The rose part and the green part always filled the whole bar together.

phases.win: one quarter lit amber, and the answer card reads 25% of 60 is 15

ladder: A quarter is one of four equal parts, not one of two.
50% is a half, so fold the bar in two with Half.
One tenth means ten equal parts, so use the Tenth key.
Halve 44, then halve that half again.
Fold into four with Quarter, then share 44 among the four parts.

phases.screen: the bar holding 80, and the question card asking for 40% of it
phases.win: four parts of eight lit, and both routes read 40% of 80 is 32

ladder: Find what one tenth of 40 is before you count lots of it.
30% is three lots of 10%, so cut the bar and find 10% of 50.
15% is 10% and then half of another 10%.
To find 10% of 40, share 40 into ten equal parts.
Light six parts for 60%, then add six of those tenths together.

phases.screen: the bar holding 2 km, and the question card asking how many metres 20% of it is
phases.win: the bar reads 2000 m in violet, and the answer card reads 20% of 2 km is 400 m
phases.traceback: the bar is relabelled in the answer's unit in violet, cut into ten, the parts needed light amber with their shares, and the line ends on the answer
ladder: Change 3 kg to grams first, using the Unit fact card.
Change 3 m to centimetres before you find 20%.
Use the Unit fact card to change 2 km to metres.
Cut the bar in grams into ten, and find what one part is.
Find 10% of the bar in grams, then take three lots of it.

phases.screen: the bar holding 800 g of flour, and the question card asking how much is left after 30% is used
phases.win: 240 g lifted off in rose, and 560 g left in green, labelled Left
phases.traceback: the used part lifts off in rose and the part left stays green, both with their amounts, and the line takes the used part away from the whole
ladder: The question asks for the juice left, not the juice poured out.
The whole garden is 100%, so take the dug part away.
Change 5 kg to grams first, then take away the 20% used.
Cut the bar, light the 40% poured out and tap Use.
Find 10% of 1,500 mL, then take as many lots as there are green parts.
The two halves are equal and together make 36.
Which number added to itself makes 36?
70 shared into ten equal parts gives one tenth.
How many tens make 70?
Light three parts, then find what one part of 50 is.
Share 50 into ten equal parts, then add three of them.
Cut, light two parts, then tap Half a tenth to keep 15% lit.
Find 10% of 60, then half of that, and add the two.
Each m is 100 cm, so multiply 3 by 100 for the bar in cm.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: the right fold is drawn, the asked part lights amber with its share written on it, and the line reads the per cent of the number
Phase 2: the bar is cut into ten, the parts needed light amber with each share written on them, and the fraction line ends on the answer
Phase 3: the bar is relabelled in the answer's unit in violet, cut into ten, the parts needed light amber with their shares, and the line ends on the answer
Phase 4: the used part lifts off in rose and the part left stays green, both with their amounts, and the line takes the used part away from the whole

voice.opening: A whole bar, ready to be folded or cut.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: fold the bar, light parts, double it, use a part or change the unit.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You found every part, and said which part was asked for.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

getState: toolId, mediaId, mode, mountPhase, phase, phases, conceptId, objectiveIds, step, steps, item, items, stage (teach, demo, ask, win, idle, summary, free), question, questionText, choices, typed, keypadOpen, tries, answered, firstTry, score, maxScore, answerShown (only after the answer), complete, questionCount, muted (the sound effects), speaking (always false: the lesson is silent), voice ("silent"), mascot, summaryRow, played, classroom, held (a classroom's parked piece of a long line), instruction (the pinned line), hint (the hint under it, or null), guideStep / guideSteps / guideOn (a guide-steps phase only), quantity, unit, to, per_cent, folds, lit, used, complete

terminalEvent.name: finished
terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first

sounds: Web Audio, no files, on in every mode (the sound button switches them): correct, wrong (soft), win at a phase end, cheer at the last, a tick when a piece snaps, and cut, settle and trade where the picture moves
